answer: Make identity cost collateral: each participant locks a bond in a public registry before routing payments. A newcomer needs vouchers from two bonded peers to reach the summit of trust and open an inlet for value; since each voucher is itself stake-backed, fake aliases cannot bootstrap for free. Sending value across a bridge between markets needs a fresh signed receipt, and replaying one slashes every backer. An attacker pays a bond per alias, forfeits it on detection, and must recruit distinct honest guarantors, so scaling the attack costs linear stake plus the trust of real agents.
